# Utility, understanding and 3D routing (verified 2026-10-21)

Dated cache, not truth. Every endpoint ID below was active on **2026-10-21**; fields and limits come from the live OpenAPI schemas and prices from each model's `llms.txt` plus the pricing API on that day. Re-verify before the first paid call (footer).
Base prices last machine-checked on 2026-10-01.

## Selection policy
1. default = quality first per use case: follow the OpenArt arena board for that use case where one exists; scores within about 15 points are ties, broken by recency, then price, then control surface.
2. Recency: a successor released on fal after the arena snapshot replaces its predecessor for the same use case (GPT Image 2.5 over GPT Image 2); arena marketing names are mapped to live endpoint IDs.
3. budget = cheapest current-generation endpoint that still does the job. Never substitute it silently for a model the user named.
4. premium = highest fidelity regardless of price; control = richest control surface for a named need (end frame, elements, multi-shot, masks, reference count).
5. No arena board (audio, 3D, utilities, training, understanding): fal catalog order within the task, newest generation in a family, and the verified schema surface decide. Every ID was active on verified_on; prices are dated.

Arena = OpenArt Arena board v1.0, snapshot 2026-09-22 (one vendor's Elo-style signal). Tiers: **default** = quality-first pick for the use case; **budget** = cheapest current-generation pick; **premium** = highest fidelity regardless of price; **control** = richest control surface for the need named in its why. Price tags in brackets: promo = promotional price with an end date in price_note; tentative = fal labels the price tentative; token-priced = billed in tokens; convert with the formula in the model's llms.txt; compute-billed = billed per compute second; cost depends on runtime; mismatch = pricing API base number differs from the llms.txt text; price_note follows llms.txt unless it says otherwise.

### `util-concat-video` - Concatenate clips
| Tier | Endpoint | Why | Price | Key limits | Media fields (`*` required) -> output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | `fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/merge-videos` Ffmpeg Api | ordered concat with optional fps and resolution normalization | compute-billed: $0.00017 per compute second (pricing API) [compute-billed] | input: video_urls: at least 2, in play order; other: target_fps 1-60; resolution preset or {width,height}; resolution_aspect_ratio_video_index picks the clip whose aspect wins | `video_urls`* -> `.result.video.url` |

- Notes: Local ffmpeg is free and faster when installed; use the endpoint when it is not, or when inputs are already CDN URLs.

### `util-mux-audio` - Put an audio track on a video
| Tier | Endpoint | Why | Price | Key limits | Media fields (`*` required) -> output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | `fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/merge-audio-video` Ffmpeg Api Merge Audio-Video | mux one audio file onto one video | $0.0002/second | other: start_offset seconds, default 0 | `video_url`*, `audio_url`* -> `.result.video.url` |

- Notes: Measured 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-21: the output is as long as the shorter input (a longer voice is cut to the picture, a shorter one cuts the picture) and the clip's own audio is replaced, not mixed.

### `util-concat-audio` - Concatenate audio files
| Tier | Endpoint | Why | Price | Key limits | Media fields (`*` required) -> output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | `fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/merge-audios` FFmpeg API [Merge Audios] | ordered audio concat (not a mix) | compute-billed: $0.00017 per compute second (pricing API) [compute-billed] | input: audio_urls: 2-5 files | `audio_urls`* -> `.result.audio.url` |

- Notes: No listed endpoint overlays (mixes) tracks; mix with local ffmpeg (amix) or place several audio tracks in util-timeline.

### `util-timeline` - Timeline compose (one picture track plus audio tracks; clips play back to back)
| Tier | Endpoint | Why | Price | Key limits | Media fields (`*` required) -> output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | `fal-ai/ffmpeg-api/compose` FFmpeg API Compose | multi-track assembly from keyframes | $0.0002/second | input: tracks[] = {id, type video / audio / image, keyframes[] = {timestamp, duration, url}}; timestamp and duration in milliseconds | `tracks[].keyframes[].url`* -> `.result.video_url` |

- Notes: Output is a bare string at .result.video_url (plus .result.thumbnail_url), not a file object. Measured 2026-09-21: one picture track per request (an image track counts as one; video plus image is a 400). Clips play back to back in keyframe order at the first clip's size and frame rate; a clip with another frame rate is not converted and plays too slow or too fast. Keyframe durations trim nothing and later timestamps in a track are ignored. Overlapping audio tracks are mixed at equal weight, each lowered. A clip's own audio survives only when the request has no audio track. Details: platform.md section 10.

### `mesh-remesh` - Remesh an existing mesh (polygon budget, quads, extra formats)
| Tier | Endpoint | Why | Price | Key limits | Media fields (`*` required) -> output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | `fal-ai/hunyuan-3d/v3.1/smart-topology` Hunyuan 3D Smart Topology | the only active remesh with a published per-call price; density levels instead of a face count, triangles or quads; its schema lists GLB, FBX, OBJ and USDZ outputs | $0.75 per generation (pricing API base: $0.015/unit) [mismatch] | input: input_file_url: GLB or OBJ, <= 200 MB, with input_file_type glb / obj; other: polygon_type triangle / quadrilateral; face_level low / medium / high. Trap: input_file_url is not marked required and defaults to fal's sample model, so a call without it bills $0.75 for the sample | `input_file_url` -> `.result.model_glb.url` |
| control | `tripo3d/tripo/remesh` Tripo3D Remesh | a numeric face budget (500-20000) and bake, which carries textures onto the new mesh; GLB, OBJ, FBX or STL in | $0.01 per unit with no unit count published: the cost per call is unknown, ask first | input: mesh_url*: GLB, OBJ, FBX or STL, <= 150 MB; other: face_limit 500-20000 (500-10000 with quad; unset = adaptive); quad forces FBX output and a 10000 default; bake default true; part_names from tripo3d/tripo/segment keeps parts separate; result carries model_urls.glb / fbx | `mesh_url`* -> `.result.model_mesh.url` |

- Notes: Order: geometry first (remesh), then texture, rig last. No schema here promises that a remesh keeps textures or a skeleton, so inspect the result before delivering it. No active endpoint takes a target format, a real-world height or a pivot since fal-ai/meshy/v5/remesh was unlisted (2026-10-05). The FBX, OBJ and USDZ slots in these schemas were not measured: take what comes back, and scale or move the pivot in a local tool.

### `mesh-rig` - Rig and animate an existing humanoid mesh
| Tier | Endpoint | Why | Price | Key limits | Media fields (`*` required) -> output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | `fal-ai/meshy/rigging` Meshy Rigging | auto-rigs a humanoid GLB from any generator; walking and running clips come with it | $0.20 per request, +$0.12 with enable_animation (pricing API base: $0.80/generation; the fal billing page showed one rig as a quarter of that, 2026-09-21) [mismatch] | input: model_url*: a GLB humanoid with clearly defined limbs, in A- or T-pose; other: height_meters default 1.7; enable_animation reads animation_action_id 0-696 (default 92, 0 = Idle) from Meshy's library at https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/animation-library, and an ID outside the range is a 422; never guess what an ID means | `model_url`* -> `.result.rigged_character_glb.url` |
| control | `fal-ai/meshy/rigging/multi-animation` Meshy Rigging Multi Animation | up to 10 clips against one rig, returned in request order | $0.20 per request + $0.12 per clip in animation_action_ids (3 clips = $0.56) [mismatch] | input: model_url* and animation_action_ids*: 1-10 distinct IDs, each 0-696, duplicates dropped; other: height_meters default 1.7; clips come back in animations[] with action_id, animation_glb and animation_fbx | `model_url`* -> `.result.animations[].animation_glb.url` |

- Notes: Animals, vehicles, props and creatures with extra limbs are not supported: say so and deliver the static mesh. Rig last. A remesh or a retexture after rigging loses the skeleton, and a pose with fused limbs rigs badly: fix the pose at generation time (Meshy pose_mode) instead. Rigging at generation time instead of here: meshy/v7.1/image-to-3d and meshy/v7.1/multi-image-to-3d take enable_rigging for the same +$0.20.

## Stale IDs -> what to use

## Verify before you pay
1. Alive? `genmedia models --endpoint_id <id> --json` must show `status: "active"` (`null` = unlisted, `deprecated`, or a 404 error = removed). If not, take the next tier, then search with `genmedia models "<name>" --no-classify --limit 10 --json` and pick the newest active match.
2. Fields? `python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/gm.py" schema <id>`: confirm names, enums and limits. It resolves the nested shapes and limits the short `genmedia schema --json` view drops; `--field <name>` prints one field in full. Parameter names do not transfer between model families.
3. Price? `python3 "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/gm.py" price <id1>,<id2> --explain` prices a whole plan in one call and returns each model's `llms.txt` Pricing paragraph as `pricing_text`; read it when `unit` is not per image, second or minute (tokens, compute seconds, units, megapixels) and for every video model. Never quote a price from this file without the date.
4. Never run `genmedia run` without an explicit endpoint ID; smart routing resolves stale defaults.

This table is regenerated by the plugin maintainers from dated routing data (verified 2026-10-21); the refresh tooling lives in the plugin repository, not in this skill. If a row looks stale, verify live as above and tell the user instead of editing this file.
